# v3.13-dev

Documentation only. No functional change.

## Clarified

- **What the `report-only` script-policy setting actually does.** The notes
  described it as suspending "the policy", which understated it in one direction
  and overstated it in another. While that setting is on, *no* Content-Security
  Policy is enforced — including the script rules it exists to test, so an
  injected script would run exactly as it does under the `legacy` setting.
  Meanwhile page-framing, content-sniffing, referrer and permissions
  protections are **unaffected**, because those are sent as separate headers.

  The documentation now says both halves plainly, names which protections lapse,
  and makes the practical advice explicit: `report-only` is a short diagnostic
  window for finding out which script is at fault, not a safer middle setting.
  If you need to run non-default for more than a few minutes, `legacy` is the
  one to use — it is looser than the default, but it does enforce.

This affects the README, the contributor documentation and the code comments in
the same place. Nothing about how the app behaves has changed.
